verses.text: Samuel told all Israel, “I've listened to everything you asked of me and appointed a king over you.
Now your king leads you. I'm old and gray, and my sons are here among you. I've lived before you from my youth until today.

Here I am. Bring any charge against me before the LORD and his anointed king. Whose ox or donkey have I taken? Who have I cheated or oppressed? From whom have I taken a bribe to look the other way? I'll pay back anything I've taken.”
They answered, “You haven't cheated us, oppressed us, or taken anything from anybody.”
He said, “The LORD and his anointed one are witnesses today that you found nothing in my hands.” They answered, “He is our witness.”
Samuel said to the people, “The LORD appointed Moses and Aaron and brought your ancestors out of Egypt.
Stand here before the LORD while I remind you of all the righteous things he did for you and your ancestors.
After Jacob went down to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the LORD. He sent Moses and Aaron, who brought them out of Egypt and settled them here.
But they forgot the LORD their God. So he sold them into the hands of Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army, the Philistines, and the king of Moab. All of them fought against your ancestors.
They cried out to the LORD, ‘We've sinned by abandoning the LORD and serving the Baals and the Ashtaroth. Rescue us from our enemies now, and we'll serve you.’
The LORD sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel. He rescued you from enemies on every side, and you lived in safety.
But when you saw King Nahash of Ammon coming against you, you told me, ‘No, we want a king to rule over us,’ even though the LORD your God was already your king.
Now look at the king you chose and asked for. The LORD has set a king over you.
If you honor the LORD, serve him, listen to his voice, and obey his commands, then both you and the king who rules you will be following the LORD your God.
If you refuse to listen to the LORD and rebel against his commands, his hand will be against you, just as it was against your ancestors.
Now stand still and watch the great thing the LORD is about to do right in front of you.
Isn't it wheat harvest today? I'll call on the LORD to send thunder and rain, so you'll see for yourselves how wrong it was in his sight to ask for a king.”
Samuel called on the LORD, and the LORD sent thunder and rain that day. The people were in awe of the LORD and Samuel.
They told Samuel, “Pray to the LORD your God for us, your servants, so we don't die. We've added to all our sins by asking for a king.”
Samuel answered, “Don't be afraid. You really did all this wrong. Even so, keep following the LORD and serve him with your whole heart.
Don't turn aside to chase worthless things. They can't help you or save you, because they're empty.
For the honor of his great name, the LORD won't abandon his people. He was pleased to make you his own.
As for me, I'd be sinning against the LORD if I stopped praying for you. I'll keep teaching you the good and right way to live.
Honor the LORD and serve him faithfully with all your heart. Think about the great things he's done for you.
But if you keep doing evil, both you and your king will be swept away.”
